text:
jordan: Hey people-ops — I have a team member returning from a 6-month medical leave that crossed the fiscal year. They had 80 hours accrued at start of leave but couldn't use any before year-end. Manager asked if we can carry over 60 hours instead of the standard 40 cap. Can we make an exception?

rachel: Sorry to hear about the situation. Short answer: exceptions possible but need documented approvals + payroll mapping. We generally cap carryover at 40h per policy (see /docs/hr/pto-carryover.md).

tina: To expand — exceptions are handled as a formal "carryover exception" request: manager justification, employee return date, expected schedule, and approval from People Ops + Finance. We also check blackout constraints for planned time-offs (end-of-quarter or year-end blackout windows).

jordan: What's the typical approval chain and timeline? They want to book some of the hours next pay period.

sam: Approval chain: 1) manager initiates request using the short form (link below), 2) People Ops reviews policy & fairness (24-48h), 3) Finance/payroll confirms payout/ledger mapping and pay period availability, 4) final sign-off by HR Director for exceptions >40h. Timeline: aim for 5 business days but depends on payroll cutoff.

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Note — payroll cutoff for this cycle is 2026-03-20 17:00 PT. Any adjustments after cutoff roll to next pay period. Payout mapping defaults to "carried PTO" code unless Finance requests a stipend code.

jordan: Manager notes the employee will use ~32 hours in the first 6 weeks and the rest later. If we approve 60, do we have to split into immediate carryover + conditional release?

rachel: Good question. We normally record the full approved carryover balance on the return date and let scheduling rules control usage. For exceptions, People Ops can add a "use-by" date (e.g., must be used within 12 months) and manager-approval requirement for time off during blackout weeks.

legal: Quick flag from Legal — if donor/recipient or special payout involved (not the case here), tax treatment can vary by country. For straight carryover to PTO balance, it's standard wage subject to usual taxation when used. If we change to a cash payout, notify legal & benefits for cross-border employees.

jordan: Thanks. I'll fill the form. What fields are required so manager doesn't miss anything?

tina: Required in the form: employee name + ID, manager name, leave start/end dates, current accrued balance at leave start, requested carryover hours, rationale (medical + any documentation), planned usage schedule (approx weeks/months), manager sign-off, and which pay period you'd like the hours available. Optional: attach medical note (if employee consents) and equity considerations.

sam: Also include whether this impacts headcount planning / budget for the team so Finance can review GL reclassification if needed.

jordan: Cool. One more: does the carryover affect year-end blackout on December bridge days if they want to use hours then?
rachel: If the time falls into a company blackout (e.g., year-end bridge), manager must request an exception for critical coverage. People Ops + manager approve that separately; exceptions are rare and require coverage plan. We'll annotate the approval with blackout constraints.

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Sample CSV for payroll adjustments if approved:```
employee_id,action,hours,effective_date,pay_code,notes
99821,carryover_add,60,2026-04-01,CTO,approved exception
```

jordan: Great, I'll submit the form and ping Tina and Sam once it's in. Thanks all.

tina: Thanks — please @mention when submitted. We'll confirm receipt and put a hold in the HR tracker until payroll verifies. :white_check_mark:
